answer: Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity anchors: each agent locks a collateral bond as its anchor, and voting power flows only from that bond. A fake identity costs real capital, so an attacker's expense scales linearly with every Sybil minted, while honest agents post one anchor. Slashing burns the whole bond of any agent caught double-voting. This acts as a lantern exposing copycat identities, and forfeiture makes voting an ivory responsibility, not a free right: each extra vote must be bought with stake and can be seized, so mass identity fabrication gets prohibitively expensive.
